transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Aditi Rao (Nova - Head of Procurement), Marcus Lee (Nova - Security Architect), Elena Torres (Nova - Finance Lead)

Summary (auto):
Quick legal/finance handoff to confirm MSA/DPA redline path, KMS/SSO integration constraints, and billing cadence for a committed pilot. SE to validate KMS/BYOK feasibility on Private deployment and Dedicated options.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redlines and non-negotiables
- KMS / BYOK / HSM and SSO/SAML flow
- Billing cadence, PO and committed spend thresholds
- SLA uptime, latency SLOs for Dedicated vs Hosted
- Next steps for pilot and security artefacts

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to make this a focused call — legal and finance handoff plus a bit of tech validation. i'm Jordan, i'm the AE on the account.
[00:12] Aditi Rao: hi, thanks. i'm Aditi. we'll be looking to close procurement by mid feb if possible. got finance and security here, so trying to resolve the key open items.
[00:20] Elena Torres: hey all, Elena from finance. main question is billing cadence, PO, and whether we need a commitment to get the pricing tier you showed.
[00:29] Priya Singh: thanks Elena — quick intro, Priya from Redwood's solutions engineering. i'll cover the KMS/SAML and the private options and call out any constraints we need flagged.
[00:37] Marcus Lee: Marcus here. security items: we need SOC2, ISO reports, and clarity on who holds keys, egress, and data residency for PHI-adjacent workloads.
[00:46] Jordan Kim: great. high level: Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for Nova's compliance needs we discussed Dedicated with customer-managed KMS or Private with bring-your-own-key. today we want to align the contract path and technical feasability.
[01:05] Aditi Rao: on contract, procurement got the MSA/DPA and flagged three asks: data residency clause for EU, KMS BYOK language, and an indemnity carveout for regulated data. can you confirm we can get those redlined?
[01:22] Jordan Kim: yes we can. we'll propose targeted redlines. note: enterprise legal sometimes wants to route BYOK language to the security team for an appendix — priya, is that how we usually do it?
[01:33] Priya Singh: yeah, commonly we append a KMS addendum. technically we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via our KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys in Dedicated and Private. small caveat: for hosted shared tenancy we offer envelope encryption but not full BYOK. that sometimes causes confusion in the mts.
[01:57] Marcus Lee: can you repeat that — hosted doesn't support BYOK? we want full key control for any PHI-adjacent traffic.
[02:05] Priya Singh: for fully-managed hosted API we don't give you the raw root key to rotate in our HSM; we support customer KMS for token encryption and per-customer wrapping, but true BYOK (where you can rotate/disable at will) is available on Dedicated and Private. there are ways to mitigate — we can enable per-request wrapping with your KMS, but that still requires some shared control.
[02:34] Marcus Lee: okay that matters. we may need Private to satisfy compliance. any perf/ops differences?
[02:40] Priya Singh: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower variance latency. Private places the control plane in your VPC or on-prem and gives you full network isolation; there is some ops overhead. both support KMS/BYOK but Private is the only one we recommend when you need full key custodianship and egress controls.
[02:58] Elena Torres: from finance — what's the delta in pricing when we move from Hosted to Dedicated or Private? is there a minimum committed spend?
[03:07] Jordan Kim: yes, Dedicated and Private typically require a reserved capacity commitment. for example a mid-sized Dedicated pool for your expected load is a monthly commit — on the order of tens of thousands per month depending on vGPU config. we can run a cost model and show committed vs pay-as-you-go.
[03:24] Elena Torres: and billing cadence — can we do monthly invoices with a PO, or is it quarterly?
[03:29] Jordan Kim: we support monthly invoicing with POs for enterprise customers; PO process and net terms are part of the commercial negotiation. if you want calendar-based monthly billing and a single consolidated invoice we can do that with finance.
[03:41] Aditi Rao: procurement also needs SLA language — uptime targets and credits. what is typical?
[03:46] Jordan Kim: standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated with clear remedy credits. Private deployments can be carved into the SLA differently depending on managed components — we can propose language for availability and runbook response times.
[03:58] Marcus Lee: on incident escalation, we need a named support path and SOC during incident triage. can you add an escalation path?
[04:07] Priya Singh: yes, we include named escalation engineers for Dedicated/Private entitlements; we'll include on-call windows and a bridge playbook. I can attach a sample incident runbook.
[04:19] Elena Torres: going back to DPA — data processing agreement: we need subprocessor list and data retention limits. is that readily available?
[04:26] Jordan Kim: yes we have a subprocessor list and standard retention clauses; we can expose the list and flag any subprocessors with foreign residency constraints. we'll attach the DPA and highlight where retention can be adjusted.
[04:40] Aditi Rao: good. for the MSA we will push the indemnity carveout for regulated data — is Redwood amenable to a limited carveout tied to the hosting mode?
[04:50] Jordan Kim: we can take that to legal. often we agree to carveouts that map to Private or Dedicated with specific operational controls. i'll note that as a commercial ask.
[04:59] Marcus Lee: technical Q — latency SLOs for chat generation at 1k tokens, what's realistic on Dedicated?
[05:07] Priya Singh: for a 1k token seq, with a 4xA100-equivalent pool on Dedicated we typically see median latencies around 300–400ms for streaming tokens after the prefix warmup; tail latency can vary. if ultra-low tail latency is required we can propose a performance tuning run and kernel-level optimizations.
[05:30] Aditi Rao: how do you measure those latencies? we need instrumentation we can trust for our SRE.
[05:36] Priya Singh: Redwood Console provides per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and tracing hooks; we can grant read-only console access for your SRE during the pilot. note: sometimes metric names are slightly different across infra providers, but we can map them.
[05:54] Elena Torres: will you provide price protection for the pilot or some discount? procurement will want a ramped pricing table and committed tier pricing.
[06:03] Jordan Kim: yes we typically provide pilot pricing then convert to committed pricing. we can present a tiered pricing sheet that maps committed spend to unit rates. i'll include a sample pricing spreadsheet.
[06:13] Marcus Lee: one more security question: audit logs and KMS access logs retention — how long do you keep them and can we pull them into our SIEM?
[06:22] Priya Singh: audit logs are retained by default for 90 days in the hosted control plane; for Dedicated and Private we can extend retention and ship logs to your SIEM via connector. KMS access logs depend on provider — if you're on a cloud KMS we surface Cloud KMS audit events; for BYOK HSM we have an audit adapter.
[06:40] Aditi Rao: sounds promising. procurement timeline: if we can get redlines and pricing this week, finance can route PO next week. is that doable?
[06:50] Jordan Kim: yes — I'll circulate the redline by Friday (2027-02-12). Priya will follow up with a KMS integration doc early next week.
[06:59] Elena Torres: great. any blockers on the technical side to start a pilot with partial datasets (non-PHI) while we work through the MSA?
[07:07] Priya Singh: no blockers. we can run a scoped pilot on Hosted with synthetic or scrubbed data. if you want BYOK/Private that'll be a separate deployment path.
[07:16] Marcus Lee: we'll plan to start pilot with scrubbed data to validate performance and telemetry.
[07:22] Jordan Kim: excellent. i'll recap action items at the end.
[07:30] -- mid-call deep dive --
[07:30] Priya Singh: tech diagram: for Dedicated w/ BYOK — traffic flows through our ingress cluster, model runtime on GPU pool, and envelopes keys with your KMS provider. to be explicit: our runtime can call your KMS for wrap/unwrap ops, but if you need to revoke keys instantly that is only available on Private.
[08:00] Marcus Lee: can the KMS calls be routed to a VPC endpoint so the KMS never leaves our VPC?
[08:06] Priya Singh: yes for Private we can route via VPC endpoints. for cloud KMS there are private endpoints and for on-prem HSM we can set up secure tunnels.
[08:16] Marcus Lee: any notable latency impact for per-request wrap/unwrap?
[08:20] Priya Singh: yes some overhead — typically 10–50ms per wrap op depending on regional KMS latency. we usually recommend caching wrapped keys when possible to reduce per-token overhead.
[08:33] Elena Torres: what about support SLAs for patching and security updates in Private mode — who owns patches?
[08:40] Priya Singh: patching split depends on the deployment. on managed Private we handle runtime patches; customers handle host OS patches if they've chosen on-prem unmanaged. we'll include an ownership matrix in the onboarding doc.
[08:54] Aditi Rao: procurement also asked about export controls and data transfer fees for EU/US transit. are there transfer fees?
[09:00] Jordan Kim: we don't charge separate data transfer fees typically — charges appear in provider egress. we can add a clause on data residency and cross-border restrictions in the DPA.
[09:10] Marcus Lee: placeholder: we need to review the subprocessor list before signing.
[09:14] Jordan Kim: absolutely. we'll attach the list and highlight unusual subprocessors.
[09:20] Elena Torres: finance question: if we do a six-month pilot on committed capacity is there a break clause?
[09:26] Jordan Kim: yes contracts typically include an initial commit period and early termination terms; commercial can propose pro-rata reductions with a termination fee. we can be flexible depending on the deal.
[09:37] -- late call clarifications and recap --
[09:37] Jordan Kim: ok quick recap of what we agreed today: 1) Redwood will provide redlined MSA/DPA with proposed carveouts for regulated data and KMS addendum by 2027-02-12; 2) Priya will deliver a KMS/SAML integration checklist and architecture diagram by 2027-02-15; 3) Finance will confirm billing cadence and PO flow by 2027-02-18; 4) Marcus will send SOC2 and key-management policy by 2027-02-17; 5) we'll schedule a pilot kickoff for the week of 2027-02-22.
[09:58] Aditi Rao: that's right. procurement will review the redlines and escalate any legal questions.
[10:04] Elena Torres: finance will review pricing spreadsheet and confirm whether we can commit to the tier.
[10:10] Priya Singh: i'll also include a sample incident runbook and console read-only access for SRE.
[10:16] Jordan Kim: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with notes and attach the MSA/DPA redline, pricing model, and the SE docs.
[10:24] Marcus Lee: thanks.
[10:26] Aditi Rao: thank you.
[10:28] Elena Torres: bye.

Post-call notes:
- Jordan to open the legal redline thread and include legal@redwood; attach subprocessor list.
- Priya to validate BYOK mechanism for Dedicated vs Hosted and provide example latency numbers with caching recommendations.
- Finance to confirm whether monthly invoices acceptable and whether they need net-30 or net-60.
